Apple has updated the privacy policy for the Apple Store app, adding terms related to a yet-to-be-launched virtual shopping assistant. Details are as follows.

Apple expands use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

According to MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page have now added a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," with the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app may in future incorporate a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses, helping users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip personally identifiable information before sharing chat content with unnamed partners that provide responses to the assistant — a strong hint that at least part of the experience will be powered by third-party models from external companies.

Chat transcripts will be kept within the app for users to revisit at any time, and will also be retained for Apple to use for business analytics. Users can choose whether to allow their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant via a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

The wording in Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially be available only in select countries and regions, likely debuting in English-speaking markets before expanding to more languages and territories.

Months before this news, Apple had already added an AI-powered chatbot to its Sales Coach app to provide sales and technical resources to its retail partners. The chatbot is accessible via the "Ask" tab and uses Apple's official training materials and documentation to answer questions.

Additionally, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" in some retail stores, using AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing staff to focus on helping customers without being distracted by note-taking.

For more information about the Apple Store app and privacy, please visit this link.
